draft.title: Government enterprises
card: A government enterprise is a business owned by a government. This can be the federal, a state or a local government. Australia Post, owned by the Australian Government, is one example.
It exists to provide a service the government wants provided, such as mail, water or public transport. It often serves everyone, even places where a private business might not make money.
Many government enterprises also aim to make a profit. Making a profit does not stop a business being a government enterprise. The profit can be paid back to the government as owner.
Ownership is the test. A public company is owned by shareholders, not the government, even though its name says public.
draft.remember: Who owns it decides it: a government enterprise belongs to a government, even when it makes a profit.

a.q: Which feature makes a business a government enterprise?
opts: It is owned by a government
Its shares are sold to the public
It never aims to make a profit
It serves customers across the whole country
a.why: A government enterprise is defined by who owns it: a government. Selling shares to the public describes a public company, which is owned by shareholders, not the government.
a.clue: Think about who the owner is.

b.q: Riverlands Water is owned by a state government. It supplies water to every town in its region and pays a profit to the government each year. What is it?
opts: A government enterprise that also aims for profit
A public company, because it serves the public
Not a government enterprise, because it makes a profit
A charity, because it serves every town in the region
b.why: A state government owns it, so it is a government enterprise. It provides a service the government wants provided and also makes a profit, which many government enterprises do. Earning a profit does not change who owns it.
b.clue: Does making a profit change who owns the business?

a.best: It is owned by a government

b.best: A government enterprise that also aims for profit
